title: Top-of-charge drift bound: how much can the anchor's CV tail move eps?
registered: 2026-10-19, before any tail fit or top-state estimate on challenge data
implementation: src/tail.py (all fitting, integration, slopes, top-state and decision logic); src/test_tail.py (synthetic tests only)
no_proxy_rule: No rule, statistic or output of this round uses P_k, any proxy label or any proxy error. The submission is never changed.

data.catalogue: wp0/cv_catalogue.csv (src/wp0_catalogue.py): 41 full charges, 8 anchors (type A) and 33 top-ups (type T)
data.cv_phase: samples from the CV start (first sample with pack >= 13.95 V and I < 19.9 A) to the CV end (last sample of the charge step, I ~ 5.1 A), inclusive
data.time_origin: t = elapsed_s - elapsed_s(CV start), in seconds
data.t_end: t at the CV end (observed); the anchor's CV end and its 5.1 A point
data.I_end: observed current at the CV end

fade.Q_fc_source: sources/r11_wp4_pack_drivers.csv column Q_fc (round 11's integral of the anchor charge), anchors 1..7

M2.starts: Iinf in {0, 0.5*I_end, 0.9*I_end}; A = I(0) - Iinf; tau in {50, 150, 400} s

M4.parametrisation: fit (A1, tau1, A2, delta) with tau2 = 3*tau1 + delta, delta >= 0, so the constraint is a box bound

models.solver: scipy.optimize.least_squares, method 'trf', x_scale 'jac', ftol = xtol = gtol = 1e-12, max_nfev 20000 per start; residual = I_model - I_obs (A), unweighted; the start with the lowest cost wins
models.amplitudes_nonnegative: all amplitudes >= 0, so every model current is non-increasing in t and the cutoff time is unique

admission.rmse: RMSE over all CV samples <= 0.15 A
admission.last_third: |mean residual over samples with t >= (2/3)*t_end| <= 0.10 A
admission.rule: a (charge, model) pair is admitted when both hold and the fit converged; non-admitted pairs are reported

C1.kind: same termination as the anchor (5.1 A)

scenarios.integral: Q_tail(k; M, C) = integral of I_M from t_end to the scenario end, in Ah; closed forms for M1-M4 (M4 cutoff time by bracketing + brentq)
scenarios.cutoff_end: the scenario end is t_c >= t_end with I_M(t_c) = I_cut; if I_M(t_end) <= I_cut then Q_tail = 0
scenarios.undefined: a current cutoff that the model never reaches (M2 with Iinf >= I_cut) is 'undefined'; it is recorded, and that model is used through C5-C7

tail_drift.delta: Delta_tail(k; M, C) = Q_tail(k) - Q_tail(1), k = 2..7
tail_drift.anchor_requirement: a (M, C) pair needs anchor 1 admitted and defined (it is the reference) and at least 5 of the 6 anchors k = 2..7 admitted and defined; non-admitted or undefined anchors are dropped
tail_drift.slope: d_tail(M, C) = Theil-Sen slope (scipy.stats.theilslopes, median of pairwise slopes) of Delta_tail(k) against fade_k over the usable anchors in k = 1..7, where anchor 1 enters as the point (fade 0, Delta 0); this equals the Theil-Sen slope of Q_tail(k) against fade_k
tail_drift.loo: leave-one-anchor-out: drop each usable anchor in turn (anchor 1 included; dropping it is a re-reference that leaves pairwise slopes unchanged) and refit; LOO range = [min, max] of those slopes
tail_drift.reported_sensitivity: d over all admitted and defined anchors without the anchor-1 requirement (not used in the decision)

T2.definition: Delta F^A_V(k) = (V30_k - V30_1) / s_top; contribution Delta eps_T2(k) = -Delta F^A_V(k)
T2.V30: pack voltage at the last rest sample before the 20 A pulse (+1800-1801 s after the CV end), from wp0/cv_catalogue.csv
T2.s_top: s_top = -(least-squares slope of pack voltage against discharged Ah) on the CK0 C/20 curve (data/checkups/CK0_reference_discharge.csv.gz) over discharged Ah in the window; positive, in V per Ah of charge content
T2.per_cell: same with each cell's V30 and that cell's CK0 slope; report the highest cell at each anchor's top (CV end and +30 min)

T3.definition: Delta F^A_R(k) = -5.1 * (R_k - R_1) / s_top (main window); contribution Delta eps_T3(k) = -Delta F^A_R(k)
T3.R: pack pulse resistance at the top = sum of round 8's per-cell R_pulse_mOhm (wp0/cv_catalogue.csv R_pulse_mOhm_r8_pack), in ohm
T3.role: consistency check only; not a member of A

top_state.slopes: d_T2, d_T3 = Theil-Sen slope of Delta eps_T(k) against fade_k over k = 1..7 (anchor 1 at the origin), with the same LOO range

topups.fit: M1-M4 with the same solver and admission rules on every top-up (and anchor 0); all reported in wp2/fits.csv
topups.monthly_series: 25 C top-ups only; month k = the anchor index of the same 25 C segment (segment 2 -> 1, ..., 14 -> 7); Q_tail(month k; M, C) = median over that month's admitted, defined 25 C top-ups
topups.role: cross-check only; not used in the decision (top-ups differ in path)
topups.reported: Theil-Sen slope of the monthly medians against fade_k, k = 1..7, labelled descriptive

ck0_comparison.compare: CK0 first C/20 sample (per-cell V under 5.1 A) vs each anchor's per-cell V at the CV end (and at +30 min) vs per-cell V at the first 10 s sample of the 20 A pulse after the 30 min rest (the step-start row that repeats the rest timestamp is skipped)
ck0_comparison.report: which cell is highest (limits the top) in each case

decision_rules_verbatim: Admitted set A = all (M, C) pairs with at least 5 of the 6 anchors k = 2..7 admitted and defined, plus T2 (main window), plus C1 (≡ 0).
Envelope = max − min over A of the median d·8.2 Ah.
Identifiability: envelope ≤ 0.30 Ah. Otherwise the outcome is O3 "not identifiable": report the envelope and exit WP3 after writing the result.

O1 "tail drift small": every member of A has |median d·8.2| ≤ 0.10 Ah, and every LOO range lies within ±0.15 Ah. This closes the tail part. SUB is unchanged, and the top-tail motivation for P_drift is removed.

O2 "tail drift material": identifiable, all members of A except C1 have the same sign, and their median |d·8.2| > 0.10 Ah. Candidate "SUB + d_tail" (d_tail = median over A without C1) is leaderboard-only.
No rule uses P_k or proxy errors.

decision_implementation.pairs: (M, C) for M in M1..M4 and C in C2..C7 (24 candidates); C1 enters A once, as a single member with d = 0 and LOO range [0, 0]
decision_implementation.median_d: the Theil-Sen slope of a member (itself the median of pairwise slopes); 'median d*8.2' = slope * 8.2 Ah
decision_implementation.loo_range: a member's LOO slopes * 8.2 Ah; 'within +-0.15 Ah' means min >= -0.15 and max <= +0.15
decision_implementation.envelope: max - min over A (C1 and T2 included) of slope * 8.2
decision_implementation.order: 1) envelope > 0.30 -> O3 'not identifiable'; 2) O1 test; 3) O2 test; 4) otherwise O3 'inconclusive'
decision_implementation.O2_median: median over members of A except C1 of |slope * 8.2|
decision_implementation.same_sign: all members of A except C1 strictly positive, or all strictly negative
decision_implementation.d_tail: median over A without C1 of the slope (Ah/Ah)
decision_implementation.comparisons: values rounded to 1e-9 before comparing to thresholds

wp3_variants.function: sources/r11_drift.py add_drift: Q' = Q + d * max(0, 100.41 - Q), applied to wp0/SUB_SOH.csv

d_values.d_min: min over A of the slope (C1 and T2 included)
d_values.d_median: median over A without C1 (= d_tail)
d_values.d_max: max over A of the slope

wp3_variants.role: leaderboard-only; never scored against proxies; written under every outcome

reported_quantities: per anchor and model: fitted parameters, RMSE, last-third mean residual, admission
M1 back-of-envelope: I_end * tau_M1 (Ah) for anchors 1 and 7, and whether M1 passes admission for them
per (k, M, C): Q_tail and Delta_tail; undefined pairs listed
T2 per window (pack and per cell) and T3; d_T2, d_T3 with LOO ranges
CK0 vs anchor top cell comparison (descriptive)

synthetic_tests.grid: 10 s sampling, t in [0, 480] s (49 samples), currents rounded to 1 mA like the data
synthetic_tests.pass: each model fitted to its own trace: every parameter within 1 % (relative) of the generator, admitted, and Q_tail within 0.01 Ah of the generator's exact Q_tail for C2-C7 where defined; the M2 case with Iinf >= I_cut is reported undefined for those cutoffs; closed-form integrals match numerical quadrature to 1e-6 Ah; Theil-Sen + LOO recover a known linear slope exactly; the decision function returns the expected outcome on hand-made O1, O2, O3 and not-identifiable inputs
